messages:
Aisha: Hey team — customer is greenlit for a 6-week POC but CISO needs explicit SLAs for throughput and data handling before execs sign. They want an internal note we can share with their legal.
Tom (Sales Eng): Got it. Are they on Hosted or Dedicated?
Aisha: They'll start on Hosted but want a path to Dedicated if latency/cost targets require it.
Ravi (Security): Need the security questionnaire answers and details on data retention, egress, and key management. Also asked about SOC2 and encryption-at-rest specifics.
Evan (RevOps): Pricing ask: they want a committed monthly unit price if they commit to 3 months of Dedicated after POC. Need a fallback pricing model during POC.
Clara (Legal): I'll need any contractual SLA wording they expect (uptime %, remedy, credits) and a short description of our data-handling flow for the doc.
Tom (Sales Eng): For throughput SLA, can we offer a 95th-pct latency goal for 512 token requests on Dedicated with a min guaranteed vGPU count? I can propose: 95th < 120ms for 512 tokens at 50 concurrent streams on a 4-GPU pool.
Aisha: The customer called out 100ms target but said they can accept 120ms if guaranteed. Do we have telemetry to back up the 120ms number?
Tom (Sales Eng): Yes, we have benchmark results on the model variant they'd use (gpt-open-xxl-quant) — I can paste a short summary.
ops-bot: benchmark report uploaded: https://redwood-internal/reports/benchmarks/3499999000-poc-brief.pdf :file_folder:
Tom (Sales Eng): I'll pull the relevant graph and add mean/95/99 numbers. POC run will use caching + batching config: `batch_size=16`, `kv_cache=true`, `max_seq=512`.
Ravi (Security): Also confirm whether they require BYOK/KMS. If BYOK, we need network design notes for Private deployment. For Hosted we can offer ephemeral keys + HSM-managed keys — will that satisfy them?
Aisha: Customer prefers BYOK for production but ok to use our hosted keys for POC. That matches their security team note.
Evan (RevOps): For POC pricing: propose $X/hour for hosted inference with a capped monthly spend and an optional conversion credit toward first month of Dedicated. I'll draft numbers.
Clara (Legal): For SLA wording, suggest the following snippet in plain language for their review: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain a 99.5% uptime for the Dedicated service, with service credits for monthly availability below 99.5%." Anyone object?
Tom (Sales Eng): That seems standard. We should add a clause about fallback to a lower-tier model in case of capacity constraints and that performance expectations may vary for longer sequences.
Aisha: Good call — customer already asked about graceful degradation. Include: "Automatic fallback to compatible model variants is used to preserve availability; performance characteristics for fallback models are documented in an appendix"
Ravi (Security): I need to provide a 1-page security summary: encryption (TLS1.2+), at-rest AES-256, SOC2 status, KMS options (hosted/HSM/BYOK), retention policy template, and audit log retention. I'll assemble.
Evan (RevOps): Action items: 1) Tom to attach benchmark excerpt (today EOD). 2) Ravi to produce 1-page security summary (tomorrow noon). 3) Clara to draft the SLA snippet and conversion credit language (tomorrow EOD). 4) I will prepare preliminary POC pricing tiers.
Clara (Legal): I'll also prepare a short confidentiality blurb and mark the doc as \"for negotiation\" — so they don't treat it as final legal language.
Aisha: I'll set up a customer sync for Thursday 11am PT to run through the doc and confirm POC acceptance criteria. Please add the acceptance criteria section: throughput target, latency 95th, datasets allowed, retention period, and success metrics.
Tom (Sales Eng): One more technical detail: they want predictable token costs per request. For the POC we can instrument token accounting and export per-request logs to a secure S3 bucket for their audit — ok?
Ravi (Security): Provided S3 export will need to be via a pre-signed, time-limited upload or cross-account replication with least privilege. I'll outline options.
ops-bot: reminder: create ticket INF-4421 for dedicated capacity provisioning if they convert.
Evan (RevOps): I'll create a draft quote with two options: POC Hosted (hourly cap) and Dedicated conversion (monthly commit with discounted unit rate + one-time migration credit).
Aisha: Thanks — let's aim to have the shareable packet (benchmarks + security summary + draft SLA + pricing) ready by Wednesday close so we can prep for Thurs sync.
Tom (Sales Eng): Acknowledged. I'll upload the excerpt and a short runbook for failover behavior.
Ravi (Security): Will do the one-pager and KMS options.
Clara (Legal): Drafting SLA language now, will post in thread when ready.
Evan (RevOps): I'll circulate draft numbers here before EOD so folks can comment.
Aisha: Perfect. tagging @customer-success later for onboarding checklist once they accept. :thumbsup:
